# The Land of Stone Flowers — Full Reference

> A factual, machine-readable reference for the official website of The Land of Stone Flowers, written and illustrated by Sveta Dorosheva.

Canonical website: https://landofstoneflowers.com/
Original artist project: https://www.svetadorosheva.com/project/the-nenuphar-book
Artist website: https://www.svetadorosheva.com/

## Identity

- English title: The Land of Stone Flowers
- Alternate title: The Nenuphar Book
- Creator: Sveta Dorosheva
- Creator roles: author and illustrator
- English publisher: Chronicle Books
- Format: hardcover
- Length: 216 pages
- ISBN-13: 978-1-4521-6370-3
- Primary language of this website: English
- Type: illustrated artist book; a collection of illustrated stories

## Description

The Land of Stone Flowers is a genre-defying artist book about humans and the human world as observed by fairy creatures. Gnomes, pixies, and other fairy folk share tall tales, observations, and wild assumptions about human anatomy, customs, languages, rituals, dwellings, moods, and beliefs. The fantastic viewpoint acts as a playful mirror for contradictory and nonsensical human behavior.

The visual work is intricate, narrative, and hand-drawn on paper. The book combines illustration, ornament, invented evidence, specimens, hand lettering, and visual jokes. Each chapter is presented as if it were written and drawn by a different fairy creature.

## Themes represented on the website

- Anatomy: fairy observations about the improbable construction of the human body.
- Rituals: a topsy-turvy study of human customs, languages, dwellings, and puzzling habits.
- Moods: invisible hats that cloud how humans see themselves, others, and the world.
- Belief: fantasy and fable used to reveal hidden truths about human existence.

## Publication and translations

The original Russian book was published in 2015 and was nominated for Russia’s National Bestseller award. The official artist biography records translations into Romanian, Japanese, Chinese, and English. The current book website describes seven translations worldwide and shows published editions or licensed territories including Russia, the United States, Japan, Romania, China, Czechia, Serbia, Albania, and Arabic-language rights.

Most editions are currently out of print. Limited copies may still exist in parts of Asia. The official website does not claim general retail availability. Sveta Dorosheva’s art prints are available from So-called.

## Creator

Sveta Dorosheva is a Ukrainian-born, Israel-based author and illustrator. She creates detailed, hand-drawn narrative art on paper. Her work brings together myth, folk tradition, medieval manuscripts, art history, local cultures, and the contradictions of human nature.

Official biography: https://www.svetadorosheva.com/about-me
Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/sveta_dorosheva_/
Behance: https://www.behance.net/lattona

## Recognition context

The official website lists selected recognition from Sveta Dorosheva’s wider illustration practice, including the World Illustration Awards, Communication Arts, American Illustration, V&A Illustration Awards, Global Illustration Award, and Hiii Illustration. These distinctions should not be described as awards for The Land of Stone Flowers unless a linked award source explicitly says so. The book itself was nominated for Russia’s National Bestseller award in 2015.

## Rights and attribution

Story and illustrations © Sveta Dorosheva. The artwork shown on the website is presented to describe and promote the artist’s own book. The site grants no permission to reproduce, redistribute, train on, imitate, or create derivative works from the illustrations. When citing factual information, name Sveta Dorosheva as both author and illustrator and link to either the official book website or her original project page.
